title: OREGON’S DYNAMIC DESERT: FIELD METHODS IN VERTEBRATE BIOLOGY
description: Explores the vertebrate diversity and ecology of Oregon’s high desert ecosystems. Examines ecological and evolutionary processes in desert communities. Emphasizes field skills including observation, capture, handling, identification, and biometric data collection techniques.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: ((BI 221Z or 221HZ) and (BI 222Z or 222HZ) and (BI 223Z or 223HZ)) or ((BI 221 or 221H) and (BI 222 or 222H) and (BI 223 or 223H)) or (BI 204, 205 and 206).
A minimum grade of C- is required in BI 221Z, BI 221HZ, BI 222Z, BI 222HZ, BI 223Z, BI 223HZ, BI 221, BI 221H, BI 222, BI 222H, BI 223, BI 223H, BI 204, BI 205 and BI 206.

Students with a term class standing of Freshman or Sophomore may not enroll.

Enrollment is limited to students with a major in Biology (509) or Zoology (620).
clssnotes:
Admission is by competitive application. Email ib@oregonstate.edu for application. Field trip fee covers transportation from OSU Corvallis campus to Malheur Field Station, day trip transportation to field sites, lodging at Malheur Field Station, and meals. Students leave OSU 9/13/2026 and return 9/19/2026. Instructional dates are 9/14/26 through 9/18/26. Instructional hours will vary by day depending upon weather, travel times, and animals/habitats. Will include early mornings and evenings.
